newsitem.title: GERMANY: Male-dominated German CDU gets women's quota.
newsitem.headline: Male-dominated German CDU gets women's quota.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), the most male-dominated of all German parties, voted on Monday to reserve one-third of all posts for women.
But lingering opposition to such a quota, which Kohl has championed for years, watered down the idea so that men could end up with more than two-thirds of all elected seats.
The change was quickly approved without debate on the first day of the CDU's annual congress to avoid the divisive arguments and failed votes of previous years.
Under the new system, the CDU, whose membership is 75 percent male, will ignore any internal ballot for party posts and candidates for elections if less than one-third of those chosen are women.
But the final result of a second ballot will be accepted even if women do not make up one-third.
CDU support is weakest among young women voters, who have been shifting allegiance to the environmentalist Greens.

Only 14 percent of CDU members of the federal parliament are women. After introducing quotas in the 1980s, the opposition Social Democrats have 34 percent women in their parliamentary party and the Greens have 60 percent.

Years of debate over political quotas have shown that many women do not want them. Most of the few young women active in the CDU reject the idea of reserving places for "token women" and say the idea is outdated.
